{{Elections in Florida sidebar}}
The '''2026 Florida gubernatorial election''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect the [[governor of Florida]]. [[Primary elections]] took place on August 18, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 9, 2025 |title=2026 State Primary Election Dates |url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2026-state-primary-election-dates |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260509222424/https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2026-state-primary-election-dates |archive-date=May 9, 2026 |access-date=August 5, 2025 |website=[[National Conference of State Legislatures]]}}</ref> Incumbent governor [[Ron DeSantis]] is [[Term limits in the United States|ineligible]] to seek re-election to a third consecutive term.

[[Republican Party (United States)|Republicans]] have won every gubernatorial election in Florida since [[1998 Florida gubernatorial election|1998]]. If he wins, Byron Donalds would become the first [[List of minority governors and lieutenant governors in the United States|African American governor]] of Florida, the second African American governor elected in the [[Southern United States]], and the first elected African American Republican governor.{{Efn|[[P. B. S. Pinchback]], the first Black governor of a state, was also the first black Republican to serve as Governor of a U.S. state, when he briefly served as [[Governor of Louisiana]] during [[Reconstruction era|Reconstruction]]. However, Pinchback was never elected governor, as he was appointed to the position after the previous Governor, [[Henry Clay Warmoth]], was removed from office.}} This is the second consecutive Florida gubernatorial election in which the Democratic nominee is a former Republican.

== Background ==
A heavily populated [[South Atlantic states|South Atlantic state]] with a large and increasingly conservative [[Hispanic and Latino Americans|Latino American]] population and the northern parts lying in the [[Bible Belt]], Florida is considered to be a moderately to strongly [[red states and blue states|red state]], having not elected a Democratic governor since 1994 nor a Democrat for president since [[2012 United States presidential election|2012]] and having moved significantly rightward in the last decade.<ref name="NYTANA">{{cite web |last1=Mazzei |first1=Patricia |date=October 29, 2024 |title=Florida Stopped Being a Swing State Slowly, Then All at Once |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/10/29/us/florida-trump-republicans-swing-state.html |access-date=March 7, 2026 |website=The New York Times}}</ref> In [[2022 Florida gubernatorial election|2022]], incumbent governor [[Ron DeSantis]] was re-elected by a 19.4% margin, a considerable improvement from his 0.4-point victory four years earlier in the [[2018 Florida gubernatorial election|gubernatorial election]] during the [[2018 blue wave]].<ref name="PartyS"/>

This was followed in 2024 by Republican [[Donald Trump]] winning his adoptive home state by a 13% margin as he won a second non-consecutive presidential term, improving his 3.4% margin of victory in [[2020 United States presidential election in Florida|2020]] and seemingly diminishing Florida's longtime [[swing state|swing-state]] and [[Florida bellwether|bellwether]] status. Republicans also control all statewide offices, a large majority of the state's U.S. House delegation, both U.S. Senate seats, and supermajorities in both houses of the [[Florida Legislature]].<ref name="PartyS">{{cite web |title=Party control of Florida state government |url=https://ballotpedia.org/Party_control_of_Florida_state_government |access-date=March 7, 2026 |website=Ballotpedia |language=en}}</ref>

=== Candidate eligibility and requirements ===
Article IV, Section 5(b) of the [[Constitution of Florida|Florida Constitution]] states that, for a person to serve as governor, they must:<ref>{{Cite web |title=Article IV, Florida Constitution |url=https://ballotpedia.org/Article_IV,_Florida_Constitution |access-date=May 13, 2023 |website=[[Ballotpedia]]}}</ref>
* Be at least thirty years old;
* Be a permanent resident of Florida for at least seven years;
* Not have served as governor for six years or more of the two prior terms.

==== Cancelled debates ====
In June 2026, the [[Republican Party of Florida]] announced that they would not be hosting a gubernatorial debate, as originally planned, later that month. The party stated that they had made the decision to cancel the debate after no candidate except Donalds met its qualifications.<ref name="Cancelled"/> The party's minimum requirements for a candidate to participate included:

* At least 10% support in a Republican party-sponsored primary voter poll
* A minimum $10&nbsp;million in raised contributions
* Over 10,000 unique individual campaign donors

The announcement drew criticism from gubernatorial candidates Collins, Fishback, and Renner, as well as incumbent Governor [[Ron DeSantis]].<ref name="Cancelled"/> DeSantis attacked the party for trying to "engineer the outcome" of the primary election and acting against "the best interest of Republican voters."<ref name="Cancelled"/> DeSantis additionally noted that he himself would not have qualified under the set criteria during his [[Ron DeSantis#2018 candidacy|2018 primary run]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Ellenbogen |first=Romy |date=June 12, 2026 |title=DeSantis hits Florida GOP over Republican primary debate |url=https://www.tampabay.com/news/florida-politics/elections/2026/06/12/florida-desantis-gop-republican-debate-donalds-fishback/ |work=Tampa Bay Times}}</ref> The ''[[Miami Herald]]'' also panned the decision, calling for a primary debate to take place.<ref>{{cite news |author=Miami-Herald Editorial Board |date=June 23, 2026 |title=Florida GOP canceled the debate, but the real story is why they did it - Opinion |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/opinion/editorials/article316224360.html |work=[[Miami Herald]]}}</ref>

On June 24, [[WJAX-TV]] announced that the planned CBS debate would be cancelled, after "a majority of the Republican candidates didn’t agree to participate." Only Fishback and Renner agreed to debate, with Collins stating that he would only accept if Donalds showed as well. Donalds refused to participate in any debate, leading Fishback labeling Donalds a "coward".<ref name="Jax">{{cite news |last=Stofan |first=Jake |date=June 24, 2026 |title=With 2 candidates refusing to commit, Action News Jax will not host GOP Gubernatorial Primary debate |url=https://www.actionnewsjax.com/news/local/with-2-candidates-refusing-commit-action-news-jax-will-not-host-gop-gubernatorial-primary-debate/3FI5T5XLNBGGRJ2YQHC5IX6TWI/ |work=Action News Jax}}</ref>

On June 25, Renner announced on X that the planned Fox 13 debate, set for July 21, had been cancelled.<ref name="Fox Cancels">{{cite tweet |number=2070193010164318251 |user=Paul_Renner |title=I just learned that the proposed Fox 13 debate in Tampa on July 21st has been canceled. That's why I called on Fox News and Newsmax to host a statewide debate. With so many voters... |author-link=Paul Renner (politician) |last=Renner |first=Paul}}</ref>
